core.name: Connector

tsdoc.title: Coordinates initial effect dependency collection and synchronous source writes.
tsdoc.summary:
The connector records source signals read while installing a receiver, then
invokes each recorded receiver when that source signal changes.
remarks:
- Dependencies are captured only during installReceiver().
- Repeated reads of one signal by a receiver register one receiver identifier.
- Receivers run synchronously in insertion order for each source signal.
see: {@link effect} - Installs receivers through this connector.
{@link BaseSourceSignal} - The signal shape that triggers receivers.

core.name: deadZone

tsdoc.title: Evaluates a callback without collecting source-signal reads for the currently installing effect.
tsdoc.summary:
The callback runs synchronously with dependency collection suspended, while
preserving its return value and error behavior.
remarks:
- The zone affects only dependency collection during an effect's immediate run.
- Reads inside the callback are evaluated normally but do not become dependencies.
- Nested zones are supported, and the prior collection context is restored if the callback throws.

params.name: callbackWithSignals
params.description: The callback that may read source or derived signals.

returns: The callback result.
see: {@link BaseSourceSignal.nonReactiveValue} - Reads one signal without collecting it.

core.name: derive

tsdoc.title: Creates a read-only lazy signal from a value-catching function.
tsdoc.summary:
The returned signal invokes the catcher when its value getter is read and
attaches generic and selected non-mutating data-specific helpers.
remarks:
- The signal has no cached value or independent update lifecycle.
- Reading value evaluates the catcher synchronously and propagates its errors.
- Source-signal reads inside the catcher are visible while an effect is installed.
- Reading nonReactiveValue evaluates the catcher without collecting its source reads.

params.name: signalCatcherFn
params.description: The function invoked by the derived value getter.

params.name: nonNullInitialValue
params.description: Optional non-null hint used only to select data-specific helpers.

returns: A read-only derived signal whose value is produced by the catcher.
see: {@link compute} - Creates a derived signal from signal-capable arguments.

template.name: T
template.description: The value type returned by the catcher.

core.name: effect

tsdoc.title: Installs and immediately runs a synchronous effect callback.
tsdoc.summary:
Source signals read during the initial callback run are permanently connected
to the returned receiver and rerun the same callback when they are assigned.
remarks:
- The callback runs once before effect() returns.
- Only source-signal reads during that initial run register dependencies.
- The returned receiver has no disposal method.

params.name: signalsCatcher
params.description: The callback whose initial source-signal reads are tracked.

returns: The receiver that the connector uses for future synchronous runs.
see: {@link signal} - Creates source signals that effects can observe.

core.name: getArrayCustomNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates custom non-mutating methods for array signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Provides the library-specific `lastItem()` and `partition()` projections,
returning results that follow the derived result type of the input.
remarks:
- `lastItem()` projects the final item without changing the base array
- `partition()` returns passing and failing groups and honors the predicate `thisArg`
- All inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results; inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results

params.name: baseArraySignal
params.description: The base array signal to access values from

returns: Custom non-mutating methods for array signals

core.name: getArrayIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates intrinsic non-mutating methods for array signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Adapts standard read-only array operations so each result has the same
derived result type as the input signal.
remarks:
- All inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results that react to the base and signal arguments
- All inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results
- Methods include element lookup, transforms, reducers, predicates, and copy helpers

params.name: baseArraySignal
params.description: The base array signal to access values from

returns: Intrinsic non-mutating methods for array signals

core.name: getArrayMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates combined methods for array source signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Combines a nested `.mutate` object with the direct non-mutating projections
used by an array source signal.
remarks:
- Mutation methods are available under `.mutate`
- Non-mutating methods are direct members of the returned object
- Every projection returns a lazy `DerivedSignal`.

params.name: baseArraySignal
params.description: The base array signal to access values from

returns: Combined methods for array source signals
see: {@link getArrayMutatingMethods} - For the nested mutation methods

core.name: getArrayMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates intrinsic mutating methods for array signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Returns the array operations that update a source signal through its
`mutateWith()` hook. Copying operations work on a fresh array before the
updated value is published to dependent effects.
remarks:
- The returned methods form the contents of a source signal's `.mutate` object
- Copy-based operations do not mutate the array returned by the signal getter
- Each successful update is published through the base signal exactly once

params.name: baseArraySignal
params.description: The mutable base signal whose array value is updated

returns: Intrinsic mutating methods for array signals
see: {@link getArrayMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods} - For the source-signal method bundle

core.name: getArrayNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates combined non-mutating methods for array signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Merges the intrinsic array projections with the library-specific projections
into the non-mutating method surface attached to array signals.
remarks:
- Every projection returns a lazy `DerivedSignal`.
- This bundle does not include mutators

params.name: baseArraySignal
params.description: The base array signal to access values from

returns: Combined non-mutating methods for array signals
see: {@link getArrayMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods} - For the mutable source bundle

core.name: getBooleanMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates mutating methods for boolean signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Returns the boolean mutation surface used to flip a mutable base signal
without exposing its lower-level `mutateWith()` implementation.
remarks:
- `toggle()` flips the boolean value
- The update is published through the base signal and notifies its effects synchronously
- Source signals expose this method under `.mutate.toggle()`

params.name: Signal
params.description: The mutable base signal whose boolean value is updated

returns: Mutating methods for boolean signals
see: {@link getBooleanSignalMethods} - For the source-signal method bundle

core.name: getBooleanSignalMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates combined methods for boolean source signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Wraps the boolean mutators in the `.mutate` namespace attached to a source
signal.
remarks:
- The only boolean-specific method is `.mutate.toggle()`
- Toggling publishes one synchronous source-signal update
- Generic logical methods are attached separately by signal construction

params.name: Signal
params.description: The base boolean signal to access values from

returns: Combined methods for boolean source signals
see: {@link getBooleanMutatingMethods} - For the unwrapped mutator object

core.name: getGenericMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates logical methods for signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Builds the `or`, `is`, and `if` method groups shared by supported signal
values. Every comparison result is a lazy derived signal.
remarks:
- `or()` selects its alternative for every JavaScript-falsy input value
- `is` methods return boolean signals returned as derived signals
- `if` methods return a `then()` selector for reactive conditional values
- Length comparisons are exposed for strings and arrays
- Measure comparisons are exposed for numbers
- All inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results; inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results
examples:
```typescript
const count = signal(5);
const logical = getGenericMethods<number>(count);
logical.is.truthy().value; // true
logical.is.greaterThan(3).value; // true
logical.if.greaterThan(10).then("big", "small").value; // "small"
```

params.name: baseSignal
params.description: The signal to add logical methods to

returns: A logical methods object
see: {@link TernaryThen} - The selector returned by `if` comparisons

template.name: T
template.description: The value type exposed by the input

core.name: getMutatingAndNonMutatingDataMethods

tsdoc.title: Selects mutating and non-mutating methods for a source signal's data type.
tsdoc.summary:
Inspects the source signal's initial non-null value, or an explicit non-null
hint, and builds the method surface appropriate for arrays, plain objects,
strings, numbers, or booleans.
remarks:
- Mutators are grouped under the returned `.mutate` object
- Non-mutating methods are direct members and follow the requested derived result type
- The optional hint permits method selection for a nullable initial value
- Unsupported primitive types receive no data-specific methods

params.name: baseSignal
params.description: The mutable base signal that selected methods read or update

params.name: nonNullableInitialValue
params.description: Optional non-null value used only to select a method family

returns: The mutating and non-mutating methods supported by the selected data type

core.name: getNonMutatingDataMethods

tsdoc.title: Selects non-mutating methods for a signal's data type.
tsdoc.summary:
Inspects the signal's initial non-null value, or an explicit non-null hint,
and returns the array, object, string, or number projection methods that
match that runtime value.
remarks:
- Array detection precedes plain-object detection
- All inputs produce `DerivedSignal` projections; inputs produce `DerivedSignal` projections
- The optional hint permits method selection when the current initial value is nullable
- Unsupported primitive types receive no data-specific methods

params.name: baseSignal
params.description: The base signal whose value the selected methods read

params.name: nonNullableInitialValue
params.description: Optional non-null value used only to select a method family

returns: The non-mutating methods supported by the selected data type
see: {@link getMutatingAndNonMutatingDataMethods} - For source-signal mutators and projections

core.name: getNumberCustomNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates custom non-mutating methods for number signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Provides the library-specific `toConfined()` projection and preserves the
derived result type of the input signal.
remarks:
- `toConfined()` clamps the value to the inclusive `[start, end]` range
- Both boundaries may be signals and participate in live dependency tracking
- All inputs produce a `DerivedSignal`; inputs produce a `DerivedSignal`

params.name: baseNumberSignal
params.description: The base number signal to access values from

returns: Custom non-mutating methods for number signals

core.name: getNumberIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates intrinsic non-mutating methods for number signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Adapts the standard number formatting methods so their results follow the
derived result type of the input signal.
remarks:
- Includes `toExponential()`, `toFixed()`, `toPrecision()`, and `toLocaleString()`
- Method parameters may themselves be signals
- All inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results; inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results

params.name: baseNumberSignal
params.description: The base number signal to access values from

returns: Intrinsic non-mutating methods for number signals

core.name: getNumberSignalMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates combined non-mutating methods for number signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Combines the intrinsic formatting projections with the custom confinement
projection used by number signals.
remarks:
- The returned object contains only number-specific non-mutating methods
- Generic logical methods are attached separately during signal construction
- All inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results; inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results

params.name: baseNumberSignal
params.description: The base number signal to access values from

returns: Combined non-mutating methods for number signals

core.name: getObjectMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates combined methods for a plain-object source signal.
tsdoc.summary:
Places shallow mutation under `.mutate` and exposes keys and property
projections as direct methods on the returned object.
remarks:
- Mutation is available only through `.mutate.set()`
- Non-mutating projections are direct members
- Every projection returns a lazy `DerivedSignal`.

params.name: baseObjectSignal
params.description: The mutable base signal whose object value is used

returns: Combined mutating and non-mutating object methods

core.name: getObjectMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates mutating methods for a plain-object source signal.
tsdoc.summary:
Provides a shallow `set()` update implemented through the base signal's
`mutateWith()` hook.
remarks:
- `set()` performs a shallow merge with the current value
- Nested objects are replaced rather than deeply merged
- Source signals expose this method under `.mutate.set()`

params.name: baseObjectSignal
params.description: The mutable base signal whose object value is updated

returns: Mutating methods for the object source signal

core.name: getObjectNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates non-mutating projections for a plain-object signal.
tsdoc.summary:
Exposes the object's keys, individual properties, and a snapshot of property
signal objects while preserving the derived result type of the input.
remarks:
- `keys()` and `get()` project through the current object value
- `props()` creates one property signal for each key present when it is called
- Every projection returns a lazy `DerivedSignal`.

params.name: baseObjectSignal
params.description: The base object signal whose properties are projected

returns: Non-mutating methods for object keys and properties

core.name: getStringCustomNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates custom non-mutating methods for string signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Provides the library-specific `deepTrim()` projection while preserving the
derived result type of the input signal.
remarks:
- `deepTrim()` trims leading and trailing whitespace
- Internal whitespace runs are collapsed to a single space
- All inputs produce a `DerivedSignal`; inputs produce a `DerivedSignal`

params.name: baseStringSignal
params.description: The base string signal to access values from

returns: Custom non-mutating methods for string signals

core.name: getStringIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates intrinsic non-mutating methods for string signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Adapts standard read-only string operations so their results follow the
derived result type of the input signal.
remarks:
- Includes character lookup, search, concatenation, padding, replacement, splitting, trimming, and case conversion
- Method parameters may themselves be signals
- All inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results; inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results

params.name: baseStringSignal
params.description: The base string signal to access values from

returns: Intrinsic non-mutating methods for string signals

core.name: getStringSignalMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates combined methods for a string source signal.
tsdoc.summary:
Places string mutation methods under `.mutate` and exposes non-mutating
string projections as direct methods on the returned object.
remarks:
- Mutation methods are available only under `.mutate`
- Non-mutating projection methods are direct members
- Every projection returns a lazy `DerivedSignal`.

params.name: baseStringSignal
params.description: The mutable base signal whose string value is used

returns: Combined mutating and non-mutating string methods
see: {@link getStringSignalMutatingMethods} - For the nested mutation methods

core.name: getStringSignalMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates mutating methods for string source signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Wraps string-producing operations so each call replaces the source signal's
value through `mutateWith()`.
remarks:
- Includes concatenation, padding, repetition, replacement, slicing, trimming, and case conversion
- `deepTrim()` trims the ends and collapses internal whitespace runs
- Each method returns `void` and publishes one source-signal update

params.name: baseStringSignal
params.description: The mutable base signal whose string value is updated

returns: Mutating string methods for use under a source signal's `.mutate` namespace
see: {@link getStringSignalMethods} - For the complete source-signal method bundle

core.name: getStringSignalNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Creates combined non-mutating methods for string signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Combines the intrinsic string projections with the custom `deepTrim()`
projection used by string signals.
remarks:
- The returned object contains only string-specific non-mutating methods
- Generic logical methods are attached separately during signal construction
- All inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results; inputs produce `DerivedSignal` results

params.name: baseStringSignal
params.description: The base string signal to access values from

returns: Combined non-mutating methods for string signals
see: {@link getStringSignalMethods} - For the source-signal method bundle

core.name: IdGenerator

tsdoc.title: Supplies monotonically increasing numeric identifiers for core objects.
tsdoc.summary:
Source signals and effect receivers read newID to obtain distinct identifiers
within the current module instance.
remarks:
- The first generated identifier is 1.
- Identifiers are never reused or reset by the public API.
see: {@link signal} - Uses identifiers for source signals.
{@link effect} - Uses identifiers for effect receivers.

core.name: signal

tsdoc.title: Creates a writable source signal.
tsdoc.summary:
The created signal stores an initial value, supplies generic logical helpers,
attaches data-specific helpers for its selected value family, and synchronously
publishes changed assignments to installed effects.
remarks:
- The initial value is copied with the configured immutable-value helper.
- Object and array assignments are exposed as copies when later read.
- nonReactiveValue returns the stored value directly and does not collect an effect dependency.
- Assigning the same stored reference leaves prevValue unchanged and warns.

params.name: initialValue
params.description: The initial value stored by the signal.

params.name: nonNullInitialValue
params.description: Optional non-null hint used only to select data-specific helpers.

returns: A writable source signal carrying the supplied value type.

template.name: T
template.description: The value type to store in the signal.

api.name: compute

tsdoc.title: Computes a derived signal from signal-capable function arguments.
tsdoc.summary:
Every argument is unwrapped with `value()` inside a derived value getter, then
passed to `computerFn` in order whenever the returned value is read.
remarks:
- The computation runs when the returned derived value is read.
- Plain arguments are read as supplied; signals are unwrapped at read time.
- Source-signal reads can be collected when the derived value is read during effect installation.
- Errors thrown by `computerFn` propagate synchronously.

params.name: computerFn
params.description: The function to call with unwrapped argument values.

params.name: restArgs
params.description: Plain values or signals matching the function parameters.

returns: A derived signal containing the function result.
see: {@link derive} - Provides the lazy derived value getter.

template.name: F
template.description: The function type used for parameter and result inference.

api.name: nullable

parameters.name: input
parameters.type:
I &
    (Extract<PlainValue<I>, Primitive> extends never ? never : unknown)

tsdoc.title: Adds generic logical helpers to a nullable primitive input.
tsdoc.summary:
The wrapper exposes `or`, `is`, and `if` operations while preserving the
derived result helpers for any accepted plain value or signal input.
remarks:
- The type constraint rejects inputs with no primitive member.
- `or` uses JavaScript truthiness, not only nullishness.
- Comparisons accept signal-capable operands.
- Result helpers are lazy derived signals, including for plain inputs.

params.name: input
params.description: A value whose plain type includes at least one primitive member.

returns: Generic helper methods specialized to the input's plain value type.

template.name: I
template.description: The concrete plain or signal input type.

api.name: promstates

tsdoc.title: Creates reactive result, error, and pending state for a promise function.
tsdoc.summary:
The returned runner marks the operation as running before invoking
`promiseFn`. Settlement updates a shared state signal whose properties are
exposed as three derived signals.
remarks:
- `isRunning` becomes `true` synchronously when the runner is called and `false` on fulfillment or handled rejection.
- Success replaces the result and clears the prior error.
- Rejection is handled into the error signal and preserves the prior result.
- Rejected values are stored without runtime validation despite the `Error` type annotation.
- A synchronous throw before `promiseFn` returns a promise leaves `isRunning` true and escapes the runner.
- Concurrent runs share one boolean and use settlement order rather than request identity.

params.name: promiseFn
params.description: The promise-returning function to execute.

params.name: initialValue
params.description: Optional initial result; current runtime initialization converts falsy values to `undefined`.

params.name: ultimately
params.description: Optional callback passed to the returned promise's `finally` stage.

returns: A readonly tuple of the runner, result signal, error signal, and running signal.
see: {@link signal} - Stores the shared promise state.

template.name: Args
template.description: The tuple of arguments accepted by the promise function.

api.name: receive

tsdoc.title: Connects several signal-capable transmitters to one mutable receiver.
tsdoc.summary:
One effect is created per transmitter. Each effect immediately copies its
transmitter into the receiver, then repeats for future changes when that
transmitter is live.
remarks:
- Initialization is synchronous; the last argument supplies the final initial value.
- Plain transmitters perform only their immediate copy.
- Source and derived transmitters remain connected through their created effect receivers.
- Passing no transmitters returns an empty array.

params.name: receiver
params.description: The source signal that receives values.

params.name: transmittors
params.description: Plain values or signals to connect, in initialization order.

returns: One effect receiver per transmitter.
see: {@link transmit} - Connects one transmitter to several receivers.

api.name: tmpl

tsdoc.title: Builds a lazy derived string from a tagged-template expression list.
tsdoc.summary:
The tag creates a derived signal, evaluates deferred functions, reads signal
values, replaces nullish results with an empty string, and stringifies every
remaining expression in template order.
remarks:
- Function expressions are called with no arguments.
- Source-signal reads inside interpolation can be collected during effect installation.
- Plain expressions are evaluated each time the derived value is read.
- A throwing function or `toString()` call propagates its error.

params.name: strings
params.description: The static template fragments supplied by JavaScript.

params.name: tlExpressions
params.description: The dynamic placeholder expressions.

returns: A derived signal containing the interpolated string.
see: {@link derive} - Provides the lazy derived value getter.

api.name: transmit

tsdoc.title: Connects one signal-capable transmitter to several mutable receivers.
tsdoc.summary:
A single effect immediately copies the transmitter into each receiver in
argument order and repeats that ordered broadcast when a live transmitter changes.
remarks:
- Receiver initialization is synchronous during this call.
- A plain transmitter performs only the immediate broadcast.
- Receivers remain independently mutable between broadcasts.
- Passing no receivers creates an effect with no signal dependencies.

params.name: transmittor
params.description: The plain value or signal whose value is broadcast.

params.name: receivers
params.description: Source signals to update in argument order.

returns: The effect receiver controlling the broadcast.
see: {@link receive} - Connects several transmitters to one receiver.

template.name: ReceiverValue
template.description: The value type accepted by every receiver.

template.name: TransmitterValue
template.description: A value type assignable to the receiver value type.

utils.name: getPlainMethodParams

tsdoc.title: Unwraps a tuple of signal-capable method arguments.
tsdoc.summary:
Data-specific helpers use this function to convert their plain and
signal operands into the native argument tuple expected by JavaScript.
remarks:
- Source-signal arguments can participate in effect dependency collection.
- Plain values remain unchanged.
- Function arguments remain functions because `MaybeSignalValues` preserves callable entries.
- The returned array preserves input order.

params.name: methodParams
params.description: Arguments to unwrap in order.

returns: A new array containing each argument's plain value.

tsdoc.title: Unwraps a signal-capable input to its plain value.
tsdoc.summary:
Structurally recognized source and derived signals are read through
their `value` getter; every other input is returned unchanged.
remarks:
- Reading a source signal through this helper can participate in dependency collection.
- Signal getters return copied object and array values according to base-signal behavior.
- Only an outer signal is unwrapped; signals nested in a plain container are preserved.
- `null` and `undefined` pass through unchanged.
- Recognition relies only on the `type` discriminator.
examples:
```typescript
const count = signal(42);
console.log(value(count)); // 42
console.log(value(null)); // null
```

params.name: input
params.description: A plain value or any base/supported signal shape.

returns: The outer signal's current value or the original plain input.
see: {@link MaybeSignal} - Describes the general accepted input.
{@link Signal} - Describes the accepted signal shapes.

template.name: T
template.description: The explicitly requested unwrapped value type.

tsdoc.title: Checks for the derived-signal runtime discriminator.
tsdoc.summary:
This structural guard tests only whether `input?.type` equals
`"derived-signal"`; it does not validate computation or disposal members.
remarks:
- Source signals, nullish values, and ordinary values return `false`.
- A plain object can satisfy this check by carrying the matching discriminator.
- The check does not read `value` and therefore does not collect dependencies.
examples:
```typescript
valueIsDerivedSignal(derive(() => 1)); // true
valueIsDerivedSignal(signal(1)); // false
```

params.name: input
params.description: The value to inspect.

returns: `true` for the derived discriminator and `false` otherwise.

utils.name: valueIsMaybeSignalValueOfStringOrArray
utils.signature:
export const valueIsMaybeSignalValueOfStringOrArray = (input: any): boolean =>
  typeof value(input) === "string" || Array.isArray(value(input));

tsdoc.title: Checks whether an unwrapped input is a string or an array.
tsdoc.summary:
The helper calls `value()` and accepts either string `typeof` or
`Array.isArray` on the resulting plain value.
remarks:
- Empty arrays return `true`.
- Nullish, numeric, boolean, and object values return `false`.
- Source-signal inputs can be collected as effect dependencies when read.
- The implementation unwraps separately for each half of the boolean expression.
examples:
```typescript
valueIsMaybeSignalValueOfStringOrArray(signal("text")); // true
valueIsMaybeSignalValueOfStringOrArray(1); // false
```

params.name: input
params.description: A plain value or structurally recognized signal to inspect.

returns: `true` when the unwrapped value is a string or any array.
see: {@link valueIsSignal} - Checks signal structure without unwrapping.

tsdoc.title: Checks whether a value carries either live-signal discriminator.
tsdoc.summary: Source and derived discriminator strings are accepted; all other values are rejected.
remarks:
- The check is structural and does not validate other signal members.
- The check does not read `value` and therefore does not collect dependencies.
examples:
```typescript
valueIsSignal(signal(1)); // true
```

params.name: input
params.description: The value to inspect.

returns: `true` for a structurally recognized source or derived signal.
see: {@link valueIsSourceSignal} - Checks only the writable discriminator.
{@link valueIsDerivedSignal} - Checks only the derived discriminator.

tsdoc.title: Checks for the source-signal runtime discriminator.
tsdoc.summary:
This structural guard tests only whether `input?.type` equals
`"source-signal"`; it does not validate the rest of the signal interface.
remarks:
- Derived signals, nullish values, and ordinary values return `false`.
- A plain object can satisfy this check by carrying the matching discriminator.
- The check does not read `value` and therefore does not collect dependencies.
examples:
```typescript
valueIsSourceSignal(signal(1)); // true
valueIsSourceSignal(derive(() => 1)); // false
```

params.name: input
params.description: The value to inspect.

returns: `true` for the source discriminator and `false` otherwise.

core.name: ArrayCustomNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Custom non-mutating methods for array signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines the library-specific last-item and partition projections for an
array signal.
remarks:
- `lastItem()` projects the final element or `undefined`
- `partition()` returns passing and failing arrays in that order
- Every result follows the input signal's derived result type

core.name: ArrayIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Intrinsic non-mutating methods for array signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines standard read-only array operations whose results preserve the input
signal's derived result type.
remarks:
- All inputs return `DerivedSignal` projections
- All inputs return `DerivedSignal` projections
- Signal-valued method parameters remain reactive for all inputs
examples:
```typescript
declare const methods: ArrayIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods<number[]>;
const doubled = methods.map((item) => item * 2); // DerivedSignal<number[]>
```

core.name: ArrayMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Combined methods for array source signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines a nested mutation namespace together with direct non-mutating array
projections.
remarks:
- Mutators are grouped beneath `.mutate`
- Projection methods remain direct members
- Live source inputs normally select `DerivedSignal` projections

core.name: ArrayMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Intrinsic mutating methods for array signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines the array operations that replace a source signal's value while
presenting familiar array method names.
remarks:
- Includes concat, copy, fill, filter, removal, insertion, reverse, sort, and splice-style updates
- All methods return `void`; results are observed through the source signal
- The containing source-signal surface exposes these methods under `.mutate`
see: {@link ArrayMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods} - The complete array source surface

core.name: ArrayNonMutatingMethods
core.signature:
export type ArrayNonMutatingMethods<T extends any[]> =
  ArrayIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods<T> & ArrayCustomNonMutatingMethods<T>;

tsdoc.title: Combined non-mutating methods for array signals.
tsdoc.summary: Combines the intrinsic array projections with `lastItem()` and `partition()`.
remarks:
- Mutation methods are deliberately excluded from this surface
- Every projection result follows the input signal's derived result type
examples:
```typescript
declare const methods: ArrayNonMutatingMethods<number[]>;
const last = methods.lastItem(); // DerivedSignal<number | undefined>
```

core.name: BaseDerivedSignal

tsdoc.title: Defines the common runtime shape of a read-only derived signal.
tsdoc.summary:
A derived signal evaluates its catcher whenever its value is read and exposes
the same runtime discriminator as other derived projections.
remarks:
- Derived signals have no identifier, previous value, or setter.
- Reads can connect source signals accessed by the catcher to an installing effect.
- nonReactiveValue evaluates the catcher without connecting those source reads.
examples:
```typescript
const doubled: BaseDerivedSignal<number> = derive(() => 2);
console.log(doubled.value); // 2
```
see: {@link DerivedSignal} - Adds generic and data-specific methods.

template.name: T
template.description: The value type produced by the signal.

core.name: BaseSourceSignal

tsdoc.title: Defines the common runtime shape of a writable source signal.
tsdoc.summary:
Source signals own a value, expose the preceding assigned value, and publish
synchronous notifications whenever an assignment changes the stored value.
remarks:
- Reading value returns an immutable-library copy for objects and arrays.
- Reading nonReactiveValue does not collect an installing effect and returns the stored value directly.
- mutateWith() computes an assignment from the current stored value.
- The declaration permits a narrower source-signal view where a wider view is expected.
see: {@link SourceSignal} - Adds generic and data-specific methods.

template.name: T
template.description: The value type stored by the signal.

core.name: BooleanMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Combined data-specific methods for boolean source signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines the `.mutate` namespace that contains the boolean toggle operation;
booleans have no separate non-mutating data-specific projections.
remarks:
- Generic logical methods are attached separately during signal construction
- The only boolean-specific operation is `.mutate.toggle()`

core.name: BooleanMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Mutating methods for boolean signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines the boolean toggle operation exposed beneath a source signal's
`.mutate` namespace.
remarks:
- `toggle()` flips the boolean value
- The operation returns `void`

core.name: Comparison
core.signature:
export type Comparison<
  GenericMethodReturn extends GenericMethodReturnType,
  P extends Primitive,
> = ExistenceComparison<
  GenericMethodReturn,
  ComparisonReturnType<GenericMethodReturn>
> &
  (P extends number
    ? MeasureComparison<
        GenericMethodReturn,
        ComparisonReturnType<GenericMethodReturn>
      >
    : {});

tsdoc.title: Composes the comparison methods available to a primitive value.
tsdoc.summary:
Always includes truthiness and equality checks and conditionally includes
ordered comparisons when the value type is numeric.
remarks: - Non-number primitives do not expose measure comparisons at the type level

template.name: GenericMethodReturn
template.description: Whether methods return signals or ternary continuations

template.name: P
template.description: The primitive value type being compared

core.name: ComparisonReturnType
core.signature:
export type ComparisonReturnType<
  GenericMethodReturn extends GenericMethodReturnType,
> = ["ternary"] extends [GenericMethodReturn]
  ? TernaryThen
  : DerivedSignal<boolean>;

tsdoc.title: Selects the result of a generic comparison.
tsdoc.summary:
Ternary comparisons return a `TernaryThen` continuation; direct comparisons
return a boolean signal returned as derived signals.
remarks: - The mapping uses a wrapped conditional to avoid distribution

template.name: GenericMethodReturn
template.description: Whether the comparison is ternary or direct

core.name: DataMethodValue
core.signature:
export type DataMethodValue<T> = [true] extends [IsExactlyAny<T>]
  ? T
  : T extends string
    ? string
    : T extends number
      ? number
      : T extends boolean
        ? boolean
        : T extends bigint
          ? bigint
          : T extends symbol
            ? symbol
            : T;

tsdoc.title: Normalizes a distributed value branch before selecting data-specific methods.
tsdoc.summary:
Literal primitive branches become their primitive base type, while any and
non-primitive branches are preserved unchanged.
remarks:
- String, number, and boolean literals normalize to string, number, and boolean.
- The any type is preserved so it does not acquire an arbitrary method family.
examples:
```typescript
type Text = DataMethodValue<"ready">; // string
type Count = DataMethodValue<1>; // number
```
see: {@link IsExactlyAny} - Identifies the any special case.
{@link NonMutatingMethods} - Selects methods from the normalized branch.

template.name: T
template.description: One member of a signal value union.

core.name: DerivedSignal
core.signature: export type DerivedSignal<T> = BaseDerivedSignal<T> & DerivedSignalMethods<T>;

tsdoc.title: Represents a read-only, lazily evaluated signal with helper methods.
tsdoc.summary:
A derived signal runs its catcher only when its value getter is read and
exposes generic and selected non-mutating data-specific helpers.
remarks:
- Derived signals do not store a previous value or expose a setter.
- The catcher is invoked for each value read; its result is not cached.
- Reads performed by the catcher can connect source signals to an installing effect.
- nonReactiveValue invokes the catcher without connecting its source reads.

template.name: T
template.description: The value type returned by the catcher.

core.name: ExistenceComparison

tsdoc.title: Defines truthiness and strict-equality comparisons.
tsdoc.summary:
Supplies `truthy()`, `falsy()`, `equalTo()`, and `notEqualTo()` with a shared
comparison result type.
remarks: - Equality methods use strict JavaScript equality semantics
examples:
```typescript
declare const checks: ExistenceComparison<
  "deriver",
  DerivedSignal<boolean>
>;
const present = checks.truthy();
```
see: {@link Comparison} - For the complete comparison surface

template.name: GenericMethodReturn
template.description: Whether methods return signals or ternary continuations

core.name: GenericMethodReturnType
core.signature: export type GenericMethodReturnType = "ternary" | "deriver";

tsdoc.title: Identifies the result style of a generic comparison.
tsdoc.summary: Selects either a direct signal result or a ternary `then()` continuation.
remarks:
- `"deriver"` selects a boolean signal
- `"ternary"` selects `TernaryThen`
see: {@link ComparisonReturnType} - For the conditional result mapping

core.name: GenericMethods

tsdoc.title: Selects the generic logical methods available to a value type.
tsdoc.summary:
Combines fallback, direct comparison, and ternary comparison surfaces based
on the input's primitive, string, array, or object shape.
remarks:
- Exact record types receive no generic methods
- Primitive-containing types receive `or`, `is`, and `if`
- Array-only types receive length-based `is` and `if` groups

core.name: HasPrimitive
core.signature:
export type HasPrimitive<T> =
  Extract<T, Primitive> extends never ? never : true;

tsdoc.title: Determines whether a type contains at least one supported primitive member.
tsdoc.summary:
Produces `true` when extracting `Primitive` from `T` is non-empty and `never`
otherwise.
remarks: - Union inputs succeed when any member belongs to `Primitive`
examples:
```typescript
type NullableString = HasPrimitive<string | null>; // true
type RecordOnly = HasPrimitive<{ value: string }>; // never
```
see: {@link Primitive} - The primitive union being extracted
{@link GenericMethods} - Where this predicate enables logical methods

core.name: IsAndIfComparison

tsdoc.title: Defines direct and ternary comparison groups for a supported value.
tsdoc.summary:
The `is` group returns direct result signals, while the `if` group returns
`then()` continuations. Length groups are added for strings and arrays.
remarks:
- Numeric primitives include ordered comparisons
- Strings and arrays include nested `length` comparisons
see: {@link LengthComparison} - The string and array length group

template.name: T
template.description: The primitive or array value type

core.name: IsArray
core.signature: export type IsArray<T> = T extends readonly unknown[] ? true : false;

tsdoc.title: Determines whether a type is an array.
tsdoc.summary: Produces `true` when the input extends a readonly array and `false` otherwise.
remarks: - Both mutable and readonly arrays satisfy this predicate
examples:
```typescript
type MutableArrayCheck = IsArray<number[]>; // true
type ScalarCheck = IsArray<number>; // false
```
see: {@link NonMutatingMethods} - Where this predicate selects array methods

core.name: IsExactly

tsdoc.title: Tests whether two types are exactly assignable in both directions.
tsdoc.summary:
Returns `true` for an exact match and `never` when either directional check
fails.
remarks: - Function wrappers prevent ordinary distributive conditional behavior
examples:
```typescript
type Exact = IsExactly<string, string>; // true
type NotExact = IsExactly<string, string | number>; // never
```
see: {@link GenericMethods} - Where exact-type checks shape method availability

core.name: IsExactlyAny
core.signature: export type IsExactlyAny<T> = 0 extends 1 & T ? true : false;

tsdoc.title: Determines whether a type is exactly `any`.
tsdoc.summary:
This guard is needed before method selection because conditional types
involving `any` can otherwise satisfy unrelated branches. For example,
`IsArray<any>` resolves to `boolean`, which must not cause an arbitrary
projected value to receive the array method surface.
remarks:
- This predicate returns true only for the special any type.
- It prevents data-method selection from treating any as a concrete value family.
examples:
```typescript
type AnyCheck = IsExactlyAny<any>; // true
type StringCheck = IsExactlyAny<string>; // false
```
see: {@link DataMethodValue} - Uses this predicate before normalizing a value branch.
{@link NonMutatingMethods} - Avoids selecting methods for any.

core.name: IsObjectLiteral
core.signature:
export type IsObjectLiteral<T> = T extends object
  ? T extends readonly any[]
    ? false
    : T extends (...args: any[]) => any
      ? false
      : true
  : false;

tsdoc.title: Determines whether a type is an object literal candidate.
tsdoc.summary:
Produces `true` for object types other than arrays and functions, and `false`
for all remaining types.
remarks:
- Readonly arrays are excluded together with mutable arrays
- Class instances still satisfy the structural object branch
examples:
```typescript
type RecordCheck = IsObjectLiteral<{ name: string }>; // true
type ArrayCheck = IsObjectLiteral<string[]>; // false
```
see: {@link NonMutatingMethods} - Where this predicate selects object methods

core.name: IsUnionAndHasOtherTypeThan
core.signature:
export type IsUnionAndHasOtherTypeThan<T, U> = [true] extends [IsExactly<T, U>]
  ? never
  : Extract<T, U> extends never
    ? never
    : Exclude<T, U> extends never
      ? never
      : true;

tsdoc.title: Detects a union that contains a target type and at least one other type.
tsdoc.summary:
Produces `true` only when `T` includes part of `U` without being exactly `U`;
all other cases resolve to `never`.
remarks: - Exact matches and unions with no matching member both resolve to `never`
examples:
```typescript
type Mixed = IsUnionAndHasOtherTypeThan<string | null, null>; // true
type Exact = IsUnionAndHasOtherTypeThan<null, null>; // never
```

template.name: U
template.description: The member type to look for

core.name: LengthComparison

tsdoc.title: Wraps comparisons for a string or array length.
tsdoc.summary: Exposes the ordinary numeric comparison surface beneath a `length` member.
remarks: - Length comparisons use the same strict and inclusive operations as numbers
see: {@link Comparison} - The nested numeric comparison surface
{@link IsAndIfComparison} - Where length checks are conditionally exposed

template.name: GenericMethodReturn
template.description: Whether methods return signals or ternary continuations

core.name: LogicalOrAlternative

tsdoc.title: Defines the fallback method available to supported primitive values.
tsdoc.summary:
The `or()` method selects an alternative for a falsy input and returns a
signal matching the derived result type.
remarks:
- The result excludes `null` and `undefined` from the original value branch
- The alternative may itself be a signal
examples:
```typescript
declare const methods: LogicalOrAlternative<string | undefined>;
const text = methods.or("fallback"); // DerivedSignal<string>
```
see: {@link GenericMethods} - The conditional method surface containing `or()`
{@link DerivedSignal} - The result returned by or().

core.name: MaybeSignal
core.signature: export type MaybeSignal<T> = T | Signal<T>;

tsdoc.title: Represents either a plain value or a source/derived signal carrying it.
tsdoc.summary:
APIs use this union when they accept ordinary inputs while allowing callers
to supply a signal whose current value should be read.
remarks:
- Only an outer signal is recognized and unwrapped.
- Plain values are returned unchanged by value().
see: {@link Signal} - The signal branch of this union.
{@link value} - Unwraps a maybe-signal at runtime.

template.name: T
template.description: The plain value type accepted by the API.

core.name: MaybeSignalValues

tsdoc.title: Converts function parameters into a tuple accepting signal-wrapped values.
tsdoc.summary:
Callable tuple elements remain callable so callback parameters are not
mistaken for value-producing signals; other elements become `MaybeSignal`.
remarks:
- Tuple positions and optionality are preserved.
- This transformation has no runtime behavior.
see: {@link PlainValues} - Extracts plain values from such a tuple.

core.name: MeasureComparison

tsdoc.title: Defines ordered numeric comparisons.
tsdoc.summary:
Supplies strict and inclusive greater-than and smaller-than methods with a
shared comparison result type.
remarks: - Comparison operands may be signals
examples:
```typescript
declare const checks: MeasureComparison<
  "deriver",
  DerivedSignal<boolean>
>;
const positive = checks.greaterThan(0);
```
see: {@link Comparison} - For the primitive comparison composition
{@link ExistenceComparison} - For truthiness and equality checks

template.name: GenericMethodReturn
template.description: Whether methods return signals or ternary continuations

core.name: MutatingAndNonMutatingMethods
core.signature:
export type MutatingAndNonMutatingMethods<T> = [true] extends [IsArray<T>]
  ? ArrayMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods<Extract<T, any[]>>
  : [true] extends [IsObjectLiteral<T>]
    ? ObjectMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods<
        Extract<T, Record<string, any>>
      >
    : [true] extends [IsExactly<T, string>]
      ? StringMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods
      : [true] extends [IsExactly<T, number>]
        ? NumberNonMutatingMethods
        : [true] extends [IsExactly<T, boolean>]
          ? BooleanMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods
          : {};

tsdoc.title: Selects the full data-specific method surface for a source value.
tsdoc.summary:
Maps arrays, object literals, exact strings, exact numbers, and exact booleans
to their corresponding source-signal method types.
remarks:
- Mutation methods are nested beneath `.mutate` where the selected type supports them
- Number values expose projections but no number-specific mutators
- Unsupported values map to an empty object type

template.name: T
template.description: The source value type used for method selection

core.name: NonMutatingMethods
core.signature:
export type NonMutatingMethods< T> = [
  true,
] extends [IsExactlyAny<T>]
  ? {}
  : [true] extends [IsArray<T>]
    ? ArrayNonMutatingMethods<Extract<T, any[]>>
    : [true] extends [IsObjectLiteral<T>]
      ? ObjectNonMutatingMethods<Extract<T, Record<string, any>>>
      : [true] extends [IsExactly<T, string>]
        ? StringNonMutatingMethods
        : [true] extends [IsExactly<T, number>]
          ? NumberNonMutatingMethods
          : {};

tsdoc.title: Selects non-mutating methods from a value's data type.
tsdoc.summary:
Maps arrays, object literals, exact strings, and exact numbers to their
corresponding projection surfaces and maps unsupported values to an empty
object type.
remarks:
- Selection priority is array, object literal, exact string, then exact number
- Boolean and unsupported primitive values have no non-mutating data-specific surface

template.name: T
template.description: The value type used for method selection

core.name: NonNullSignalValue
core.signature:
export type NonNullSignalValue<S> =
  S extends SourceSignal<infer SS>
    ? SourceSignal<NonNullable<SS>>
    : S extends DerivedSignal<infer DS>
      ? DerivedSignal<NonNullable<DS>>
      : S extends null | undefined
        ? never
        : NonNullable<S>;

tsdoc.title: Removes nullish values while preserving the surrounding signal kind.
tsdoc.summary:
Plain values use ordinary nullish exclusion; source and derived signal inputs
are rebuilt with null and undefined removed from their value types.
remarks:
- A wholly nullish plain type becomes `never`.
- Runtime values are not validated or transformed by this type.
see: {@link Signal} - Signal kinds preserved by this transformation.
{@link nullable} - Adds generic helpers to nullable primitive inputs.

template.name: S
template.description: The plain or signal type to make non-nullish.

core.name: NumberCustomNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Custom non-mutating methods for number signals.
tsdoc.summary: Defines the library-specific inclusive confinement projection.
remarks:
- `toConfined()` clamps values to `[start, end]`
- Both bounds may be signals
- The result follows the input signal's derived result type
examples:
```typescript
declare const methods: NumberCustomNonMutatingMethods;
const confined = methods.toConfined(0, 10); // DerivedSignal<number>
```

core.name: NumberIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Intrinsic non-mutating methods for number signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines standard number-formatting operations whose results preserve the
input signal's derived result type.
remarks:
- Includes exponential, fixed, precision, and locale-aware formatting
- Formatting arguments may be signals
- All inputs return `DerivedSignal` results; inputs return `DerivedSignal` results
examples:
```typescript
declare const methods: NumberIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods;
const fixed = methods.toFixed(2); // DerivedSignal<string>
```

core.name: NumberNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Combined non-mutating methods for number signals.
tsdoc.summary: Combines standard number formatting with the custom confinement projection.
remarks:
- Generic logical methods are not part of this data-specific type
- Every result follows the input signal's derived result type

core.name: ObjectMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods
core.signature:
export type ObjectMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods<
  T extends Record<string, any>,
> = { mutate: ObjectMutatingMethods<T> } & ObjectNonMutatingMethods<
  T
>;

tsdoc.title: Combined methods for object source signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines a nested shallow-mutation namespace together with direct key and
property projections.
remarks:
- Mutation is exposed beneath `.mutate.set()`
- `keys()`, `get()`, and `props()` remain direct members

core.name: ObjectMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Mutating methods for object signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines the shallow object update operation exposed beneath a source signal's
`.mutate` namespace.
remarks:
- `set()` performs a shallow merge with the current value
- Nested values are replaced rather than deeply merged
see: {@link ObjectMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods} - The complete object source surface

core.name: ObjectNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Non-mutating methods for object signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines key and property projections whose results preserve the input
signal's derived result type.
remarks:
- `keys()` projects enumerable string keys
- `get()` projects one named property
- `props()` creates a property-signal object for keys present when called

core.name: PlainValue
core.signature:
export type PlainValue<I extends MaybeSignal<unknown>> =
  I extends Signal<infer T> ? T : I;

tsdoc.title: Extracts the contained type from a signal or preserves a plain type.
tsdoc.summary:
This is the type-level counterpart of the runtime `value()` helper for a
single `MaybeSignal` input.
remarks:
- Every signal kind is unwrapped through `Signal<infer T>`.
- Plain inputs remain unchanged.
examples:
```typescript
type Count = PlainValue<BaseSourceSignal<number>>; // number
```

template.name: I
template.description: The plain or signal input type.

core.name: PlainValues

tsdoc.title: Extracts contained value types from a tuple of signal-capable inputs.
tsdoc.summary:
Each tuple element is matched against `MaybeSignal` and replaced by the
inferred underlying value type.
remarks:
- Tuple positions are preserved.
- This transformation is used by `compute` and method-parameter helpers.

template.name: T
template.description: The tuple of signal-capable values to unwrap.

core.name: Primitive
core.signature: export type Primitive = string | number | bigint | boolean | null | undefined;

tsdoc.title: Represents the primitive values supported by generic logical methods.
tsdoc.summary: Includes strings, numbers, bigints, booleans, `null`, and `undefined`.
remarks: - Objects, functions, symbols, and arrays are not members of this union
see: {@link HasPrimitive} - For detecting members of this union
{@link GenericMethods} - For the methods selected from primitive values

core.name: Receiver

tsdoc.title: Represents a synchronous effect receiver.
tsdoc.summary:
A receiver has a stable identifier and invokes its effect callback through
run() when a connected source signal is written.
remarks:
- Receivers do not expose disposal or lifecycle controls.
- The connector uses id to deduplicate repeated reads of one source signal.

core.name: Signal
core.signature: export type Signal<T> = SourceSignal<T> | DerivedSignal<T>;

tsdoc.title: Represents either writable or derived signal form.
tsdoc.summary:
This union is the common input accepted by helpers that only need to read a
signal value.
remarks:
- Source signals are writable; derived signals are read-only.
- Both forms carry a type discriminator and a value getter.
- A signal with a narrower value type is assignable to the corresponding wider signal type.
see: {@link SourceSignal} - The writable member of this union.
{@link DerivedSignal} - The read-only member of this union.

template.name: T
template.description: The value type exposed by the signal.

core.name: SignalConnector

tsdoc.title: Defines the internal registry used to connect source-signal reads to effects.
tsdoc.summary:
Source-signal getters register the effect currently being installed, and
source-signal writes synchronously invoke each registered receiver.
remarks:
- This is exported for the core implementation; applications normally use effect() instead.
- Dependency registration occurs only while an effect is first installed.
see: {@link Receiver} - The callback registered for source-signal changes.
{@link effect} - The public API that installs a receiver.

core.name: SignalType
core.signature: export type SignalType = "source-signal" | "derived-signal";

tsdoc.title: Identifies a source or derived signal at runtime.
tsdoc.summary:
The discriminator is used by the value utilities to recognize the two signal
implementations without reading their values.
remarks:
- source-signal identifies a writable source signal.
- derived-signal identifies a read-only derived signal.

core.name: SourceSignal
core.signature: export type SourceSignal<T> = BaseSourceSignal<T> & SourceSignalMethods<T>;

tsdoc.title: Represents a writable signal with generic and data-specific helpers.
tsdoc.summary:
A source signal stores its value, exposes the preceding assigned value, and
synchronously runs effects that read it while those effects were installed.
remarks:
- Objects and arrays are copied when read through value.
- nonReactiveValue reads the stored value without registering an installing effect.
- Assigning the identical stored reference warns and does not notify effects.
- The available data-specific helpers are selected from the initial value or hint.
- A narrower value view is assignable to a matching wider source-signal view.
see: {@link DerivedSignal} - The read-only computed signal form.

template.name: T
template.description: The value type stored by the signal.

core.name: StringCustomNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Custom non-mutating methods for string signals.
tsdoc.summary: Defines the library-specific `deepTrim()` projection for string signals.
remarks:
- `deepTrim()` trims the ends and collapses internal whitespace runs
- Its result follows the input signal's derived result type
examples:
```typescript
declare const methods: StringCustomNonMutatingMethods;
const trimmed = methods.deepTrim(); // DerivedSignal<string>
```

core.name: StringIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Intrinsic non-mutating methods for string signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines standard read-only string operations whose results preserve the input
signal's derived result type.
remarks:
- Covers character lookup, search, concatenation, padding, replacement, splitting, trimming, and case conversion
- All inputs return `DerivedSignal` projections
- All inputs return `DerivedSignal` projections
examples:
```typescript
declare const methods: StringIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods;
const upper = methods.toUpperCase(); // DerivedSignal<string>
```

core.name: StringMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Combined methods for string source signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines a nested mutation namespace together with direct non-mutating string
projections.
remarks:
- Mutators are grouped beneath `.mutate`
- Projection methods remain direct members

core.name: StringMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Mutating methods for string source signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Defines string-producing operations that replace a source signal's value and
return `void`.
remarks:
- Includes concatenation, padding, repetition, replacement, slicing, trimming, and case conversion
- `deepTrim()` trims the ends and collapses internal whitespace runs
- The containing source-signal surface exposes these methods under `.mutate`
see: {@link StringMutatingAndNonMutatingMethods} - The complete string source surface

core.name: StringNonMutatingMethods

tsdoc.title: Combined non-mutating methods for string signals.
tsdoc.summary:
Combines the intrinsic string projections with the custom `deepTrim()`
projection.
remarks:
- Mutation methods are deliberately excluded from this surface
- Every projection result follows the input signal's derived result type

core.name: StringReplaceParameters

tsdoc.title: Represents the parameters accepted by string replacement methods.
tsdoc.summary:
Pairs a search value with either a literal or callback replacement value for
the mutating and non-mutating string method surfaces.
remarks: - Each tuple member may be signalified through `MaybeSignalValues` at call sites

core.name: StringReplaceSearchValue

tsdoc.title: Represents values accepted as the search operand of string replacement.
tsdoc.summary:
Supports literal strings and objects implementing JavaScript's
`Symbol.replace` protocol.
remarks: - Regular expressions satisfy the protocol-based branch
see: {@link StringReplaceValue} - For the corresponding replacement operand
{@link StringReplaceParameters} - For the complete parameter tuple

core.name: StringReplaceValue

tsdoc.title: Represents values accepted as the replacement operand of string replacement.
tsdoc.summary:
Supports a literal replacement string or a callback that computes the
replacement from the matched substring and capture arguments.
remarks: - The callback follows the native `String.replace()` argument convention
see: {@link StringReplaceParameters} - For the complete parameter tuple

core.name: StringSplitParameters

tsdoc.title: Represents the optional parameters accepted by string splitting.
tsdoc.summary: Contains an optional protocol-aware separator and an optional result limit.
remarks: - Omitting both values follows native `String.split()` behavior
see: {@link StringIntrinsicNonMutatingMethods} - The method surface using this tuple

core.name: StringSplitSeparator

tsdoc.title: Represents values accepted as a string split separator.
tsdoc.summary:
Supports literal strings and objects implementing JavaScript's `Symbol.split`
protocol.
remarks: - Regular expressions satisfy the protocol-based branch
see: {@link StringSplitParameters} - For the complete split parameter tuple
{@link StringReplaceSearchValue} - For the analogous replacement protocol

core.name: TernaryThen

tsdoc.title: Defines the final branch selector for a ternary comparison.
tsdoc.summary:
`then()` chooses between two maybe-signal values and returns a signal matching
the original derived result type.
remarks: - Both branch values participate in dependency tracking for all inputs
examples:
```typescript
declare const branch: TernaryThen;
const label = branch.then("yes", "no"); // DerivedSignal<string>
```

api.name: StringSignalDeriverTemplateExpressions

tsdoc.title: Describes the expression list accepted by the `tmpl` tag.
tsdoc.summary:
Expressions may be signal objects, zero-argument deferred functions, or plain
values. The broad plain-value branch intentionally permits any JavaScript value.
remarks:
- Functions are invoked whenever the returned derived value is read.
- Signal values are read when the returned derived value is read.
- Nullish expression results are rendered as empty strings.
examples:
```typescript
const expressions: StringSignalDeriverTemplateExpressions = [
  signal("Ada"),
  () => 42,
```
